T0666.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography
T0666.definition: Post-quantum cryptography is a family of public-key algorithms designed to remain secure against both classical and quantum computers.
T0666.description: PQC uses structures such as lattices, hashes, and error-correcting codes instead of RSA and elliptic-curve assumptions vulnerable to Shor's algorithm. NIST has standardized algorithms including ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and SLH-DSA. Migration must address larger keys and signatures, compatibility, performance, and implementation side channels, often through hybrid deployment during transition.
T0666.usageExample: The organization piloted a hybrid PQC key exchange in TLS to reduce the future quantum-decryption risk to long-lived sensitive data.
